relationship.owner_rule: WALL_NORMAL_CONSTRAINT owns only the normal axis during contact; tangent motion and body custody remain with A.
relationship.support_rule: wall contact never silently becomes full support; rear/lead foot ownership is explicitly authored.
relationship.release_rule: normal contact may release only after lead-foot catch and a held peel-load threshold.

timing.note: 1s/2s/4s mean ONES/TWOS/FOURS display classes, never seconds; all Contact014 decisive timing is INFERRED.

keys.role: Establish a displaced asymmetrical free state with the wall present but irrelevant.
keys.arc: Root starts left of the wall with rear-biased support; front hand is deliberately low and inside reach.

keys.role: Body-first approach: rear support drives while the lead side opens a crooked path toward the surface.
keys.arc: Pelvis travels right on a shallow rise; front hand arcs ahead and high without reaching the seam.

keys.role: Eligibility before acquisition: hand is near the seam while rear foot and lowered COM store the normal load.
keys.arc: Root is still left of the seam; front hand stops short; rear foot is the world-readable anchor.

keys.role: Acquire the wall in the normal axis only; contact is a unilateral constraint, not body custody.
keys.arc: Front hand meets the seam inside committed reach while the rear pin prevents a floaty farthest-reach snatch.

keys.role: Denied normal displacement becomes torso/pelvis compression rather than dead wall-sticking.
keys.arc: Hand stays on the same seam cell while head and pelvis fold down-left around the fixed rear foot.

keys.role: The relationship changes class: normal stays owned by the wall while tangent becomes explicitly free.
keys.arc: Contact seam migrates downward two rows; root does not advance through the wall.

keys.role: Persistent contact carries a visible vertical slide; the body pays with knee/torso compression and secondary-arm lag.
keys.arc: Hand/seam drop three rows while x stays locked; pelvis drops and retreats slightly, proving tangent motion under normal constraint.

keys.role: A new ground support catches the vertical debt while wall contact persists; support ownership changes without contact release.
keys.arc: Lead foot lands farther right as pelvis overshoots down; wall seam remains acquired at a lower address.

keys.role: Lead support turns the body away while the hand still owns normal contact; this is a held release threshold, not release yet.
keys.arc: Pelvis rises and shifts left while the hand remains at the seam; force normal magnitude visibly falls.

keys.role: Separately authored release: the hand breaks normal contact after the foot has earned a peel vector.
keys.arc: Hand leaves the seam first while pelvis is already driving away; release is not reverse interpolation.

keys.role: Body recoil overshoots away from the wall while the former contact arm remains late and high.
keys.arc: Pelvis crosses left slower than head/chest; front hand trails near the old relationship line.

keys.role: Secondary limbs arrive late; split support catches recoil without erasing the previous downward slide.
keys.arc: Rear hand/foot trail behind the chest while the root arrests at a new address.

keys.role: Recover asymmetrically near—but not against—the wall, preserving spatial and support debt instead of resetting.
keys.arc: Final stance remains closer to the wall and more lead-biased than K0.
